I worked for the OC Sochi 2014, the Olympic games held in Russia... we did the biathlon... I think it was about 100 of us as a biathlon team... at some point we decided it would be cool to make pins for every team member. Something unique, a lil initiative not connected to the Olympic symbolics but rather to the core team that made it possible... It sounded affordable... we found the guys.. and then we learned about the price of the mold to make those pins.. and how there need to be at least 10 thousand of them, to make it actually 'affordable'... the glaze and other stuff was peanuts comparing the to price of the mold... So, in order to get them, we had to vote... and we agreed to keep them unique, so we only made one hundred of those for the price of 10 thousand... and we agreed that the mold will be sent to us too, cause we didn't want any replicas. So, I own an overpriced lapel pin that nobody else but 100 people thought was important)

The idea of competing against non-consumption deserves way more attention. Every major technology wave didn't just replace existing work, it unlocked demand that didn't exist before. AI will automate tasks, but it'll also create products and services that simply weren't practical before. That's a much more useful way to think about the future than asking whether AI replaces jobs. We've had some great discussions around this at ABTalks too.
